What DirectX 12 means for gamers and developers
Put some extra tape on your glasses before reading this article boys.
I prefer OpenGL, so I'm not very excited for this.

Basically the OpenGL version of DirectX 12.

AMD donated Mantle, and then Valve, whoever makes Unity, several other engine companies, whoever it was who does OpenGL standards, and AMD all worked together to make Vulkan from Mantle.

It is supposed to be similar to DirectX12 in performance, and should require a lot less driver overhead.

Yep. It supposedly already has support in several major engines, including Source 2 and Unity. The only problem is that so far nobody knows what the standard is because it hasn't been officially released yet.

I wonder how many devs will actually be able to take advantage of the power that low-level API's offer. There is a reason we don't write programs in assembly anymore, and that's because it's really hard to do. Personally, I think DX12 and Vulkan will separate the men from the boys so to speak. Developers who are talented enough to properly implement and optimize their low-level code will be able to make incredible things while everyone else will lag behind. Hopefully, we'll see a resurgence in technical ability in the gaming industry, since all we seem to hear about is the artsy parts lately. I have nothing against the more art-oriented parts of the industry, I just feel like the technical side has been overshadowed in recent years.
